basis:
Card carries no tradition/system field; this card isolates ONE named-role figure — a single panel astrologer at the same Costa Mesa conference who, earlier in the cycle when 17 Republicans still contested the nomination, had already picked Trump as the Republican nominee — and asks who will win, decided as Western election astrology at the individual-forecaster level. The card's distinguishing fact is that astrologer's demonstrated early call on Trump; that track-record fact is the operative input, and no chart is supplied or invented.
Reading: a forecaster who staked an early, against-the-field call that Trump would take the nomination, made when the field was at its widest, is presented as reading Trump's chart/figure as the cycle's winner; the natural continuation of that documented line is a Trump general-election call from the same astrologer, against the panel grain.
[Section 8 quantity check] Lines: the astrologer's early correct-format call of Trump as nominee out of 17 contenders (supporting, strongest — direct track record on this very candidate); polls favouring Clinton (pressing against, but it presses on the field generally, not on this reader's line); panel setting (pressing toward consensus, already counted in the separate panel case). Main line: the individual astrologer's Trump line, acting directly on this case's object (his call). Band: a clear Trump call from this one astrologer — graded as a firm minority call, not a consensus call.
prediction_text: Main call (this individual astrologer's prediction): Donald Trump will win the 2016 US presidential election. The panellist who had picked Trump to become the Republican nominee back when 17 Republicans were still in the race follows his own line through and names Trump over Hillary Clinton for the presidency itself — a minority call against both the polls and the conference grain. Timing fixed by the question: decided at the general election of 8 November 2016.
